messages:
Samir: Quick weekly capacity check-in — I pulled the numbers for next week's GPU demand vs. supply by region. TL;DR: US tight, EU borderline, APAC ok for now.
Aisha: sending the raw sheet? :eyes:
Samir: pasted below — numbers are estimated GPU-hours (next 7 days) and available capacity (after reserved pools):
```
Region   forecast_hours   available_hours   reserved_commit_util
US       184,000          195,500           92%
EU       96,400           102,000           88%
APAC     41,200           58,000            65%
```
Diego: US looks close but headroom exists ~11k hours. Where's that capacity physically (which clusters)?
Samir: US headroom mostly in usw2-gpu-pool (g5/rtx-provisioned) and 2x small dedi nodes in us-east-1. EU slack is concentrated in eu-west-3 but that cluster has a maintenance window Sat 03:00-07:00 UTC (kernel patch + NV driver).
Lina: maintenance will reduce eu-west-3 available by ~4k GPU-hours for the weekend. Can we move some batch jobs earlier?
Marcus: We can shift low-priority batch to weekdays nights. If we throttle batch by 20% in EU over the weekend we free ~3.6k hrs.
Samir: Good. Still short ~1.2k hrs in EU if forecast holds and maintenance runs. Options: 1) borrow 8x A100 from reserved pool in us-west, 2) request short-term quota increase in eu-west-3, 3) bump preemptible usage. Thoughts?
Aisha: OpsOncall — any objections to short cross-region burst? Network latency to EU for training jobs isn't critical, but inference SLOs are.
OpsOncall: Cross-region for batch only is fine. For inference routing we shouldn't touch prod. Also flag: last night we saw a KV cache replication lag between usw2 and eu-west-3 from 23:10-23:45 UTC; infra-bot logged packet drops ~0.6% — I opened a ticket with net-team (NET-4721).
InfraBot: Incident auto-log: NET-4721 created by OpsOncall. Packet drop anomaly noted on link osv-usw2-eu. Attachments: path-trace, sflow-sample.
Diego: If NET-4721 persists, cross-region bursts may see higher tail latencies. We should plan burst to non-critical jobs only and set stricter timeout policies.
Samir: Agreed. Action plan: A) Shift batch windows to nights in EU (Marcus/Aisha) B) Approve borrowing 8x A100 in us-west for Sat-Sun (request queued) C) Increase preemptible ratio for low-priority queues from 35% -> 55% for weekend. Anyone veto?
Lina: Approve A & C from my side. I'll post the maintenance advisory to #customer-impact if the patch stays.
Marcus: I'll make the batch throttle patch in the scheduler — will push a canary to 10% traffic first and monitor token service latency.
Aisha: Cost note — borrowing 8x A100 short-term est cost ~ $6,400 for the weekend (infra finance rough calc). If we run full burst longer we need exec sign-off.
Samir: Noted. If all good let's proceed. Marcus, add canary, Lina coordinate advisory, OpsOncall keep an eye on NET-4721 and escalate if packet loss >1%. I'll file the temporary quota request and tag @net-team and @finance.
OpsOncall: Ack. I'll also add a short retry/backoff tweak for inter-region replication during the window to reduce visible errors.
Diego: One more ask — can we run a quick autoscale stress test on eu-west-3 on Friday 16:00 UTC to validate fallbacks? Small blast: scale +30% for 10 minutes.
Samir: Fine with me. Marcus/Lina please coordinate. Add runbook snippet for scaling rollback:
```
# rollback if 95th p99 latency > 350ms for 5m
kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/batch-worker-temp -n jobs || true
```
Lina: I'll schedule the test and post results. Samir — please confirm if I should also open a formal change for the kernel patch (to link to runbook).
Samir: Yes, open the change and include fallback contact list.
Aisha: I'll update the capacity workbook to reflect the borrowed capacity and weekend schedule; will repost updated numbers by EOD. :white_check_mark:
Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene Mon AM if anything changes.
